label: FP
reason: Alert is a false positive. Although CodeQL traces taint from user input (getParameterNames() at line 45) to the sink (printf at line 64), the resolved sink value ('bar') is derived from the HTTP parameter NAME, not the VALUE. HTTP parameter names are restricted by the Servlet specification/RFC 3986 to alphanumeric characters and limited symbols ([A-Za-z0-9._~!$&\'()*+,;=-]), precluding script tag injection. Additionally, the logic only populates 'param' if the parameter VALUE matches a constant ('BenchmarkTest01423'), ensuring 'bar' is either a safe parameter name or an empty string. Thus, the sink value is structurally safe.

evidence.note: Taint flows from getParameterNames() (line 45) to 'name', then to 'param' (line 60) only if value matches constant, then to 'bar' (line 74) and finally to 'obj' (line 64) which is printed to writer. Since 'param' holds the parameter NAME (not value), it cannot contain XSS payloads.
